name: AHW
source: Advanced Hypersonic Weapon (U.S. Army/Sandia) - conical glide body of the SWERVE lineage (SWERVE with improved thermal protection). Entry model per Acton, Science & Global Security 23 (2015): 191-219. Distinct from the C-HGB, which is a separate biconic reentry vehicle.
notes: Conical glide body, SWERVE heritage (AHW = SWERVE with better TPS). This is NOT the C-HGB - they are different systems; the C-HGB is a biconic RV (see C-HGB.rv.json). Lower L/D (1.5) than the HTV-2 waverider (2.6), consistent with a blunter cone. The aero numbers here (L/D 1.5, beta 10,000) are REPRESENTATIVE estimates for a conical glide body, not a published fit: Acton fit only the HTV-2, and there is no comparable public AHW aero fit. Built as the entry-style companion to the HTV-2 RV: this one defaults to equilibrium_glide_acton (Acton's explicit three-phase entry: high-AoA broadside direct-reentry at beta_S -> pull-up -> equilibrium glide), whereas HTV-2 defaults to the gentle dynamic_equilibrium_glide capture. glider_beta_entry_kg_m2 = 20 is an Acton-style entry beta_S placeholder and only affects the equilibrium_glide_acton path. NOTE Acton's own reading: after the pull-up the HTV-2 and AHW trajectories are 'probably quite similar' - the per-RV difference modeled here is the entry/capture maneuver, not the glide.
